summary: Feed s125_double to APM is degraded: 68.5% of TCP sessions are one-way (APM requires bidirectional) and 16.4% duplicate packets detected. Both faults reduce APM transaction correlation and waste capacity.

findings.root_cause: Only one direction of most TCP sessions is reaching the APM. Most likely asymmetric routing with TAP/SPAN on single link or packet broker load-balancing/policy splitting client->server and server->client to different tool ports without bidirectional aggregation.
findings.impact_on_tool: APM needs_both_directions=true to correlate requests/responses and measure latency. With 85/124 sessions one-way, APM cannot build complete transactions, latency/error breakdowns will be incomplete and many transactions will be missed or flagged as incomplete.

recommended_fix.why: Configure packet broker to aggregate both directions of each flow and hash symmetrically to the same APM tool port so request and response are seen together.

findings.root_cause: 16.4% duplicates (247/1504) indicates same packet delivered twice - typical when both sides of a link are SPAN-mirrored or two TAPs feed the same broker without deduplication, or 's125_double' feed is aggregated from overlapping sources.
findings.impact_on_tool: APM will count duplicate transactions/packets, inflating throughput and response counts, skewing latency histograms, and wasting its 10Gbps processing budget on redundant data.

recommended_fix.why: Enable packet-broker deduplication window to drop identical packets arriving within milliseconds from overlapping TAP/SPAN sources before delivery to APM.
